title: Find another angle with same position
text: Notice that $$\frac{13\pi}{6}$$ is larger than one full rotation of $$2\pi.$$ We can subtract $$2\pi$$ (which is equivalent to $$\frac{12\pi}{6}\$\$)$$ $$to$$ $$find$$ $$a$$ $$simpler$$ $$angle$$ $$on$$ $$the$$ $$primary$$ $$unit$$ $$circle$$ $$that$$ $$is$$ $$at$$ $$the$$ $$same$$ $$position$$.

title: Calculate the angle
text: $$\frac{13\pi}{6}-\frac{12\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{6}.$$ Since the angles correspond to the same point on the unit circle, they have the same $$y$$ coordinate. Meaning $$\sin\left(\frac{13\pi}{6}\right)=\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right).$$

title: Evaluate the special value
text: Recall your unit circle. The angle $$\frac{\pi}{6}$$ is in the first quadrant, where the $$y-$$ coordinate is positive. The $$y-$$ coordinate (sine) at this angle is $$\frac{1}{2}.$$
